messages:
nora: Quick kickoff: we need a low-friction staged compatibility workflow for model swaps. Goal: reduce emergency pins and make migration predictable for customers. Ideas welcome.

carl: High level: three-stage path: preview -> opt-in bridge -> retire. Preview = read-only evaluation for customers. Bridge = time-limited pin with SLA tiers. Retire = deprecation notice + final cutover.

harry: Agree. Important to include measurable pass/fail checks at each gate. Proposal:
- preview gate: smoke tests + 100 curated prompts for semantic parity
- bridge gate: embedding drift <= 0.025 and manual approval
- retire gate: canary run 24h at 10% traffic + error <0.5%

len: Infra constraints: every active bridge costs persistent KV + index slots. Suggest defaults and hard caps:
```
per_account_bridge_limit: 2
global_bridge_soft_cap: 120
default_bridge_ttl_days: 90
```
If soft cap reached, auto-waitlist new requests and notify infra team.

olivia: Product UX notes: surface a "compatibility score" on model pages (0-100) showing embedding drift, latency delta, and semantic score. Include CTA: "Request bridge" with fast/standard/extended options. Fast = 30d, standard = 90d, extended = 180d (paid).

nora: For incentives, CS suggested migration credits: 2 weeks free tokens + one migration workshop for standard bridge. If enterprise chooses extended, require contract amendment.

carl: We need a transparent cost pass-through calc for long bridges. Ops: propose surcharge = reserved_memory_gb * $X / month plus a 10% ops handling fee.

len: Ops-bot: Current pinned_count=35; soft_cap headroom OK. Note: memory reservations currently estimated at ~1.2GB per pinned variant.

harry: CI/benchmarks: create a reusable job template that runs automatically when a model is proposed for bridge. Steps:
1) run 200 seed prompts for semantic diff
2) compute embedding cosines on golden vectors (n=1000)
3) synthetic p95 under request QPS for 15m
Fail statuses should block bridge requests in the UI.

olivia: UX detail: make the bridge request modal require: justification, requested_ttl, lane selection, and attach bench artifacts (link to CI run). Also add a checkbox: "I accept potential surcharge".

carl: Governance: bridge exceptions >180d must go to a 3-owner approval board (product + infra + legal). Temporary emergency bridge (14d) allowed with incident tag and email to board.

nora: Notifications: add expiry reminder cadence: 60d, 30d, 14d, 7d, 1d. Include consolidated list for CS weekly digest so they can pro-actively engage customers.

harry: Monitoring: set up a sampled-diff pipeline for bridged traffic (1% sample) that computes daily regression rate and alerts if >2% for 24h. Also auto-trigger rollback if user-facing error spike >1% in 1h.

len: Billing hooks: emit bridging_event with metadata (account, model, ttl, reserved_memory_gb) so billing can invoice monthly. We'll add a backfill script to populate historic pins.

olivia: Comms: draft short FAQ for customers explaining lanes, costs, and how to request. Also prepare a canned CS script for negotiation: trade migration credits + short pin vs extended paid contract.

nora: Action items
- Harry: CI template + regression sampler spec (ETA 3d)
- Len: infra quota + billing hook + cap enforcement (ETA 4d)
- Olivia: console mock + customer FAQ (ETA 5d)
- Carl: approval board flow + external wording draft (ETA 2d)

ops-bot: Created tracking ticket RW-PL-7744 and assigned to @nora.

carl: One more ask: add a machine-readable bridge policy file in the catalog repo so infra + product can onboard new models programmatically. Example fields: allowed_lanes, region_restrictions, max_ttl.

harry: Good call. We'll add a GH PR template for model owners to fill when submitting new model versions.

nora: If no objections I'll convert this into an epic and schedule a planning session. Call out any concerns now.

len: No objections from infra side.

olivia: No objections from product UX.

harry: No objections from ML.

carl: Ok from legal ops - will coordinate external wording with legal.

ops-bot: Reminder: RW-PL-7744 tracking epic created.
